Jamie: Ran an nsys timeline on the serving binary (commit abc123) with model=gpt-8k-quant, seq=4096, batch=1. Seeing repeated KV restore/evict traffic and a bunch of small GEMMs interleaved — looks like HBM spikes and cache thrash. attaching notes and qdrep link :thinking:
Rachel: Can you share the nsys command + which kernels were selected? Iirc we switch kernels at seq>2048 so that might be related. :eyes:
Jamie: Cmd I used:
```
nsys profile --output=kv-4096 --trace=cuda,osrt -f true --stats=true \
  --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite ./serve --model gpt-8k-quant --seq 4096 --batch 1
```
Kernel selector chose matmul_algo_Y for seq>=2048 (workspace-constrained path). For 4096 the timeline shows: repeated `kv_restore` (memcopy/L2_copy), `kv_evict`, then tiny `gemm` kernels. HBM read peaks ~900-1200 GB/s during the restore bursts.
Devin: Did you run nvprof or collect memcopy counters? Need dram_read/dram_write and l2_hit ratios.
Maya: I grabbed counters: dram_read ~= 9.6e11 bytes over a 30s window (peaks ~1.1 TB/s). L2 eviction rate is high, L2 hit ratio drops when the restore spikes happen -> signs of thrash from scattered KV accesses.
Oliver: Could be our KV layout. We currently interleave heads across blocks which looks fine for small seqs but at large seqs access pattern scatters across HBM pages. Random accesses cause many L2 misses and force repeated DRAM reads.
Rachel: Two axes to try: (1) change KV physical layout to contiguous per-key block (reduces scatter), (2) prefetch N subsequent blocks before running attention for current token. Also kernel_selector should consider memory read amplification, not just FLOPS/workspace.
Jamie: I ran a microbench that toggles KV layout + prefetch. Random-access baseline vs contiguous+prefetch: runtime improved ~18% on the microbench and HBM peak reduced from ~1.05 TB/s to ~420 GB/s on the same workload. Latency tail improved ~2.5x.
Devin: Nice. Can you paste the microbench command and the tiny repro so I can run it on our infra?
Jamie: Microbench repro (KV-only):
```
./kv_microbench --layout=random --seq 4096 --iters 200  # baseline
./kv_microbench --layout=contiguous --prefetch=8 --seq 4096 --iters 200  # opt
```
I pushed csvs/nvprof outputs to perf drive: https://perf.internal/reports/1778123456 (qdrep + nvprof csvs + microbench results).
Maya: Timeline screenshots show kernel gaps where we do host stalls waiting for memcpy streams to finish. Overlapping prefetch+compute reduces that. Also noticed that for quantized kernels we do extra unpack steps that increase memory reads; quantized math reduced compute time but memory steps moved to the critical path.
Oliver: So quantized path trades compute for memory, which is bad if memory is the bottleneck. We should surface a heuristic: prefer quantized kernels only if estimated HBM traffic < threshold.
Rachel: Actionable list: (1) add contiguous_kv_mode + opt-in prefetch flag to runtime (owner: Devin), (2) update kernel_selector to include estimated HBM read metric (owner: Rachel), (3) add an nsys-based perf test for seq>2048 to CI (owner: Jamie), (4) investigate quantized unpack cost and optimize or gate it (owner: Oliver). I'll create tickets.
Devin: I'll prototype contiguous_kv_mode and run microbench on A100/RTX combos. Expect to push a small patch to the runtime by EOD.
Jamie: FYI I also reproduced this on a dedicated host (different driver) — kernel choice + layout both matter. With selector tweak + prefetch, the combined win was ~22% end-to-end on the microbench.
Maya: Filing perf regression check: if selector flips to alg_Y for >2048 seq, ensure we run a quick KV microprobe to estimate read amplification before full rollout.
Rachel: Good. Also add a short doc entry in eng-runtime/README about KV layout tradeoffs so oncall can triage these HBM spikes faster.
Jamie: TL;DR: large seqs cause KV-induced HBM thrash. Prefetch + contiguous layout + selector tweak = significant improvement. Uploading qdrep/nvprof now. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: New perf report uploaded: https://perf.internal/reports/1778123456/qdrep (qdrep + nvprof csvs).
Oliver: I'll start a ticket to analyze quantized unpack kernel; might be able to fuse unpack+matmul for some quant formats.
Devin: starting work on runtime patch, will post results in this thread.
Jamie: Thanks all — will drop a short runbook snippet once we confirm CI tests.
